Baby Hearts in Crisis PART 3 - PE Cath Lab

By: Tarryn Crossman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
When we did our last story we were promised that the Cath Lab would be up and running by Feb 2020. They are now saying maybe Oct 2020, but more likely Feb 2021

I have the official waiting list for paediatric catheterization from Dora Nginza 2020 (from Estelle)
There are 52 children on it.
The list does not include cold elective cases that can wait 6 months – 1yr from the last time they were seen. Which for many was before COVID

Dr’s notes say:
18 in urgent need of large L/R shunts at risk of developing irreversible pulmonary hypertension, 3 of which already have PH
These patients with PH will die. I counted 5 cases of PH on the list – but I will confirm

10 of them have down syndrome – this increases their chances of getting PH

Lulu’s daughter Zenade has down syndrome. She is 4 years old and should have had her second heart surgery in the beginning of 2019
(She is such a strong passionate mom, she literally just broke my heart.)
She sleeps with Zenade on her chest all night so she can feel if she stops breathing. Because if she puts her down on one side for too long she turns blue, so she can’t put her to sleep alone.
“I am always crossing my fingers that she isn’t no more”
Facts: whole family just got covid. Dr’s at Dora said don’t bring her in if she is sick because she will get sicker.
She has been unable to get Zenade’s medication as the dora pharmacy is closed due to covid and the clinics don’t have it. She managed to beg and borrow money and had to buy the medication privately this month.
Zenade’s Dr at Dora said to her two weeks ago: find other mothers, mobilise and go to Bisho. We have been begging the government and they are doing nothing. I can’t help you.

Case study 2 - 2 year old with PH due to no treatment


Further information:
This was Dr Pepeta’s life work and now without him putting on pressure there is no-one. Dr Adele Greyling who resigned shortly after our first story is willing to speak now though, she was in contact with Pepeta a few weeks before he died to find out what is happening with state paediatric patients that need Caths

Confrontation needs to be to the national minister of health – as per Nans suggestion.
We have asked ECDH twice now and they just lie.

Script:


When JOSHUA VAN DE MERWE was just a baby, doctors in the Eastern Cape diagnosed him with severe congenital heart disease and he had his first lifesaving surgery
Elmarie: when he was born they said he wouldn’t survive but he has
Joshua is now urgently in need of his final surgery but Because in the Eastern Cape the cath lab needed to save the lives of state Paediatric patients with congenital heart has not been operational for two years, he has to wait

The starting point of any heart treatment is a cath lab, which is a specialised theatre. It’s a basic tool for a cardiologist today and is used to diagnosis heart disease. It’s also used for life saving non-invasive surgical Procedures done on the heart. In October 2018, the Cath lab in Port Elizabeth which SERVed the ENTIRE Eastern Cape PROVINCE broke.

When we first met Joshua and his Mother Elmarie Van der merwe IN 2019, She was DEEPLY concerned about the lack of medical support available to Joshua

2019 Elmarie: In the past if needed too I could rush off to a hospital and now there is nothing – Crying

That was over a year ago. But Elmarie is not alone. Lulu Sifuba’s Daughter Zenanda was diagnosed with complicated congenital heart disease and down syndrome she also needs lifesaving surgery
Lulu: every time to go there they postpone, My heart is sore

Dr Adele Greyling was the head of Paediatric cardiology when the issues with the cath lab started

2020: ADELE: This equipment has got a limited lifespan. Which is about 10 years. This lab was older than 10 years and we had in fact been telling them for quite a few months if not a year that we were having issues with the equipment. So I believe that they could have planned for at this.

In January 2019 Three months after the cath lab stopped working the provincial department of health finally ordered a new laboratory
But by March when we spoke to the HOD Dr thobile MBengashe the equipment had still not arrived

2019: HOD: 29th of mARCH ITS LANDING AND WE NEED 9 WEEKS TO PUT IN IT. tAKE THE old one out and put the new one in. The Cath is going to be in place in 9 weeks


9 weeks later the lab was not operational as promised. In July 2019 we returned to find that the equipment had arrived, but it was now sitting outside the hospital in shipping containers
Again the department was adamant that they would have the lab fully operation in a few months

2019: Rolene: Our predicated completion date and handover to us is the 9th September

LINK: But that was almost a year ago and still nothing is ready
When we returned to Port Elizabeth this past week, the Eastern Cape Department of health declined to an on camera interview, they also refused us access into the Catheterization Lab.

n a text message to our producer the departments spokesperson Siyanda Mabana claimed that all the equipment has been installed and that there is just minor specialised work left to be done. He blamed the contractors that they appointed, for the delays.
The company in question was unreachable, as their landline has been disconnected and their emails are bouncing back.

2019 Pepeta: Patients that require a cath lab will die without this service

The late Dr Lungile Pepeta setup the first ever paediatric cardiology unit at PE provincial hospital back in 2009.
We interviewed him when we first begun our investigation

DR: Pepeta
Gives us the amount of people with Congenital heart disease in the country and in the EC
65-70 000 people in EC with Congenital HD

Dr Andile Nxele who was trained by Dr Pepeta, he is now the clinical head of paediatric cardiology in Port Elizabeth
They keep diagnosing, but they can’t do anything.
VO: Joshua’s condition has begun to dramatically deteriorate over the past few weeks

Elmarie Joshy is spider man
She’s concerned

Due to her concern ElmariE raised the funds to take Joshua to see a private cardiologist

He said that if he was a private patient we would have been doing the caths in two weeks

Elmarie: Longer he waits worse gets and heart failure is his future

Andile: I am sure J is blue and needs our help. But losts of other patients that look like him

Dr Adele Greyling was Joshua’s primary caregiver while she was head of paediatric cardiology in PE, she resigned in June of 2019

We had a waiting list when I resigned for surgical procedures
If we operated at capacity that we were with one to two to patients a week we could would have taken us five years easily just to catch up with the waiting list
I couldn’t see how they were going to get better and I couldn’t bear waiting for them to improve

The current waiting list is still around 150 patients in any given week. But It goes up and down as babies with congenital heart disease are born

Andile?: We haven’t done much since last year. Been only doing new urgent patients
Haven’t touched the ones form last year

From April – October 2019 the department had a public-private agreement with Netcare where 48 urgent patients from the list of about 150 managed to get treatment.

LINK: In October 2019 the private-public agreement ended And Port Elizabeth began sending patients to the state Catherization Laboratory at Nelson Mandela academic hospital in Mthatha, but only 12 paediatric patients have been sent from PE to Mthatha since October.
Because they have been waiting for treatment for so long, many children on this list have already developEd Pulmonary Hypertension, which is increased congestion in the lungs. If left untreated Pulmonary hypertension eventually becomes irreversible
Andile: When a child develops irreversible PH That child can no longer be helped. That child can no longer have surgery that defect can no longer be repaired because the heart will fail. So the patient is treated palliatively
Children with down syndrome have a higher chance of getting pulmonary Hypertension, which is why when Zenande was only a few months old she had her first operation. But that was almost 4 years ago and the longer Zenanda waits the more her quality of life decreases

Lulu: Zenanda has to sleep on her chest so she can feel she is breathing and alive
Andile: She is one of the patients that is waiting surgery. But I don’t know how long she can wait
Mac: if she doesn’t this surgery what will happen to her
Lulu: She will die. She is going to leave me

Desperate to get answers we contacted the National Department of health’s spokesperson Mr Maja and highlighted everything we had seen in Port-Elizabeth. He was shocked and offered to organise an on camera interview, but until now we have had no response to numerous attempts to contact him

Elmarie: pure rage against the department. Sick of being lied to. Petrified for my child
2 years down the line and there is still no functioning cath lab. No one has been held accountable and no-one has apologise
Lulu: speak to gov?
Beg them and ask them to give Zenande and other children a chance to live. To repair that lab because there is something they can do about this

After our interview with Lulu she told us she received an anonymous call from a man claiming to be from the health department in bisho. She says He asked her to not allow her interview to be broadcast until the cath Lab was fixed

The new envisioned date for the completion of the Cath Lab according to the provincial department will be November 2020.
Until then aLL paediatric heart patients on this waiting list will just have to live in hope.

Dr Pepete’s commitment to saving the lives of children with congenital heart disease never wavered. He died of covid -19 in July

Adile:Pepeta’s legacy is falling apart because he wanted all children to be treated
